title: FlatBuffers (flat binary serialization)
summary: FlatBuffers is a zero-copy serialization format by Google. A FlatBuffer: root table offset (4 bytes, relative to the buffer start), then tables. Each table: vtable offset (relative, signed 32-bit), then fields. Vtables: size (2 bytes), number of fields (2 bytes), then field offsets (2 bytes each). Strings: 4-byte length + UTF-8 data + NUL padding. Vectors: 4-byte length + elements.

structure.meaning: Offset from buffer start to the root table.
vtable offset (soffset32, signed) + field data (scalars, offsets to strings/vectors/tables).
vtable size (uint16) + number of fields (uint16) + field offsets (uint16 each, 0 = absent/default).
Length (uint32) + UTF-8 bytes + NUL terminator (padded to 4-byte alignment).
Inline fixed-size data (no vtable, no indirection).

ext.example_decoded: FlatBuffer: root offset 16, empty table with vtable
notes: FlatBuffers requires no parsing/unpacking: access fields directly via offsets.
Vtables enable backward/forward compatibility (missing fields default to 0).
FlatBuffers is used by Android, game engines, ML (TensorFlow Lite), and high-performance systems.
Unlike protobuf, FlatBuffers does not need a schema at runtime (the vtable encodes the layout).
